lines.trans: With the Chef everything would have been different!
Darling, I can explain everything right now!
Alright, quickly stop your wild imagination!
At least look, Maxim forgot about his grief.
Max, actually you are to blame for everything yourself.
You had no business kissing Sasha back then.
And I am not even arguing with that.
Well, it is a mistake that you give up so easily.
It seems to me that divorce is too harsh a punishment.
Especially for such a minor offense.
Yes, our former lawyer stepped in right away!
It would be great if people were put on trial for cheating!

examples.text: Не мог же я такое рассказать!
examples.trans: I could not possibly tell that story!

examples.text: Никто меня ещё так не любил!
examples.trans: Nobody has ever loved me like this before!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, fine, shallow, petty').

examples.text: Тем более за такое мелкое преступление.
examples.trans: Especially for such a minor offense.

examples.text: Ну, у каждого есть свои мелкие недостатки.
examples.trans: Well, everyone has their own minor flaws.

examples.text: Вы мелкими буквами не читаете.
examples.trans: You don't read the small print.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'crime, offence' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тем более за такое мелкое преступление.
examples.trans: Especially for such a minor offense.

examples.text: Он подозревается в новом преступлении.
examples.trans: He is suspected of a new crime.

examples.text: Это серьёзное преступление.
examples.trans: This is a serious crime.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И она сразу сказала мне да!
examples.trans: And she immediately said yes to me!

examples.text: Луи, быстро неси сюда рюмки!
examples.trans: Louis, quickly bring the shot glasses here!

examples.text: Тогда нам тем более нужно выпить!
examples.trans: Then we have all the more reason to drink!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лучше спокойно сидеть на нашей кухне.
examples.trans: It is better to sit quietly in our kitchen.

examples.text: Все они хотели помешать нашему счастью.
examples.trans: They all wanted to stand in the way of our happiness.

examples.text: Я нашёл дорогу в ваши добрые сердца.
examples.trans: I found the way into your kind hearts.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('former, ex-').

examples.text: У меня тёща бывшая чемпионка страны.
examples.trans: My mother-in-law is a former national champion.

examples.text: Да, наш бывший юрист сразу вступился!
examples.trans: Yes, our former lawyer stepped in right away!

examples.text: Слушай, ты помнишь бывшую жену Нагиева Кристину?
examples.trans: Listen, do you remember Nagiyev's ex-wife Kristina?

meanings.note: Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common masculine noun meaning 'lawyer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да, наш бывший юрист сразу вступился!
examples.trans: Yes, our former lawyer stepped in right away!

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть юрист.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always lawyer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.text: И она сразу сказала мне да!
examples.trans: And she immediately said yes to me!

examples.text: Мы же сразу тебе это говорили.
examples.trans: We told you that right from the start.

examples.text: Да, наш бывший юрист сразу вступился!
examples.trans: Yes, our former lawyer stepped in right away!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тупиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'stand up for, step in'.

related.gloss: not to stand up for (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и вступиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and stand up for on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют вступиться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to stand up for.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Было бы здорово, если бы за измены судили!
examples.trans: It would be great if people were put on trial for cheating!

examples.text: Ты адвокат? Здорово!
examples.trans: You're a lawyer? That's great!

examples.text: Здорово, поздравляю.
examples.trans: Great, congratulations.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А вот если бы ты меня убил?
examples.trans: And what if you had killed me?

examples.text: Если бы меня вдруг не стало?
examples.trans: If I were suddenly gone?

examples.text: Папа, а если бы она тебе отказала?
examples.trans: Dad, and what if she had turned you down?

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'мена'). Common feminine noun meaning 'infidelity, cheating' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Было бы здорово, если бы за измены судили!
examples.trans: It would be great if people were put on trial for cheating!

examples.text: Обычный поцелуй не является изменой!
examples.trans: An ordinary kiss does not constitute infidelity!

examples.text: Согласен, поцелуй — это настоящая измена.
examples.trans: I agree, a kiss is real infidelity.

судить.gloss: to judge, to try in court

meanings.en: to judge, to evaluate, to put on trial
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'удить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to judge, to try in court', paired with 'осудить'.

examples.text: Может, лучше обсудим это в постели?
examples.trans: Maybe we should discuss this in bed instead?

examples.text: Было бы здорово, если бы за измены судили!
examples.trans: It would be great if people were put on trial for cheating!

examples.text: Итак, подсудимый целовался с Сашей на складе.
examples.trans: So, the defendant was kissing Sasha in the storage room.
